editorial:
You are stuck in a high-rise elevator with strangers, and the lights keep going out. Every time they come back on, someone is hurt or dead. The movie turns a simple ride into a tense guessing game, because one of these people is not human. You will watch security guards and a detective try to help from outside, while the trapped group turns on each other. It feels like a locked-room mystery with a dark twist, and the short runtime keeps the story moving. The setup is simple, but the fear comes from not knowing who to trust.

The acting is solid, especially from the detective who carries the emotional side of the story. The pacing is quick, with little wasted time, and the elevator scenes create real pressure. The downside is that some twists feel a little too neat, and a few characters are thin. Still, if you like short horror thrillers that keep you guessing, this is a fun pick. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or buy the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the detective realizes the last survivor is not the Devil. The old woman in the elevator is the real threat, and she has been pushing the group toward violence. After the lights go out one last time, she reveals herself and tries to claim the detective's soul. He survives by confessing a past mistake and asking for forgiveness. The Devil leaves, the elevator opens, and the detective walks away changed.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves short, tense horror thrillers.
